questions.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
questions.statementMd:
Given an integer array `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array that contains each distinct value exactly once, in the same order.

The classic version asks you to do this in place with two pointers. Here you return the resulting array, but the same idea applies.

**Constraints**

- `1 <= nums.length <= 100000`
- `-10000 <= nums[i] <= 10000`
- `nums` is sorted in non-decreasing order.

python.driver:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys, json
    _args = [json.loads(_l) for _l in sys.stdin.read().split("\n") if _l.strip() != ""]
    _out = Solution().removeDuplicates(*_args)
    print(json.dumps(_out, separators=(",", ":")))

tests.explanation: 1 appears twice and is kept once.
Five distinct values remain, in their original order.

questions.title: Majority Element
questions.statementMd:
Given an array `nums` of size `n`, return the majority element.

The majority element is the one that appears **more than** `n / 2` times. It is guaranteed to exist.

Can you solve it in linear time and constant extra space?

**Constraints**

- `1 <= nums.length <= 100000`
- `-1000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000`
- A majority element always exists.

python.driver:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys, json
    _args = [json.loads(_l) for _l in sys.stdin.read().split("\n") if _l.strip() != ""]
    _out = Solution().majorityElement(*_args)
    print(json.dumps(_out, separators=(",", ":")))

tests.explanation: 3 appears twice out of three elements.
2 appears four times out of seven.
